summary: This incident report reviews how telecommunication networks were restored after five natural disasters occurring between September 2023 and January 2024: a hurricane, floods in Sierra Leone, California wildfires, Midwestern tornadoes, and a Mumbai monsoon. It describes the technologies used, such as portable cell towers, drones, mesh networks, COWs/COLTs, satellite hybrids, and underwater repair, and quotes the leaders involved. It concludes that technology, planning, and collaboration between governments, companies, and communities are improving disaster response.
one_line: Case studies of five disasters from September 2023 to January 2024 show the technologies and teamwork used to restore telecommunication networks.
key_facts: Hurricane Helena made landfall on the southeastern coast of the United States on September 10, 2023, with winds up to 130 miles per hour.
Bob Jennings, a field operations director for ATN, said the immediate action after Hurricane Helena was deploying portable cell towers and satellite phones for emergency responders.
After Hurricane Helena, ATN and other providers used drones with high-definition cameras and sensor arrays to assess damage, and fiber optic cables were airlifted to bypass severed lines.
Torrential rains caused severe flooding in Sierra Leone on October 4, 2023, submerging telecommunication facilities.

Dr. Amira Kanu, a disaster recovery specialist, led a mesh network approach in Sierra Leone using existing Wi-Fi hotspots and solar-powered make-shift relay stations, which was cost-effective and sustainable.
The California wildfires of November 2023 destroyed cellular towers and fiber optic lines, isolating communities.
A joint task force including telecom veteran Paul Rodriguez used Cells on Wheels (COWs) and Cells on Light Trucks (COLTs) to provide immediate but limited cellular service in California.
Fire-retardant cabling materials, fire-resistant coatings for cell towers, and improved predictive analytics were introduced as preventive measures after the California wildfires.
On December 2, 2023, powerful tornadoes hit the midwestern United States ("Tornado Alley"), dislodging cell towers and disrupting service for hundreds of thousands.
Eric Brown of Temporal Networks led a recovery using an advanced remote command center and data analytics to redirect traffic, and integrated with first responders' communication channels.
Temporal Networks and other firms added satellite-based systems to reinforce terrestrial networks, creating a hybrid system.
Heavy monsoons caused flooding in Mumbai, India, on January 19, 2024, paralyzing the telecommunication grid.
Chief technician Aarav Mehta said divers repaired submerged conduits that automated machines could not reach, and inflatable pylons temporarily raised cables above the water.
Mehta credited Mumbai's rapid response to pre-monsoon planning, including extra cable length laid for rerouting and elevated flood-immune control rooms.
